::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 21st [1893]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Lambeth Palace Library  2344 f 176
:::

Dear [Mr Riley](people/person_1239.qmd)
Have you Mr [H H Gibbs](people/person_558.qmd)’s name-?  He is either at St Dunstans, Regents Park or at Aldenham Elstree  I should think no one would be more earnest in the cause than he. I would also mention the publisher -  [A D Innes](people/person_744.qmd)31 Bedford Street Strand.  Old Mr [Alexander Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd) I am sure would but I am not so sure of his sons though his partner Mr [G L Craik](people/person_379.qmd) would, I believe   I am much obliged to [Mrs Riley](people/person_2121.qmd) for writing to me, I am sorry I was so stupid.

Of course you know Mr Gibbs’s name as MP for the City in the last Parliament and as a Bank Director[^1]

yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Riley was probably trying to raise money for some charitable purpose.
[^2]: Henry Hucks Gibbs (1819-1907) was MP for the City of London 1891-2, which dates the letter.
